DOCS-ENTPOL-002: Enterprise AI controls and organization settings govern feature, agent and model access and use, including a CLI-access example.

DOCS-ENTPOL-003: Enterprise-level policies are set before organization-level policies; organization controls cannot be interpreted in isolation. DOCS-ENTPOL-004: Most enterprise policies allow explicit enablement, disablement or delegation to organizations; this is not an unconditional least-privilege default. DOCS-ENTPOL-005: Cloud-agent access is an exception allowing an enterprise to choose the exact organizations receiving access.

DOCS-ENTPOL-006: Enterprise-assigned users are not covered by Let organizations decide through an organization seat. DOCS-ENTPOL-007: A separate Policies for enterprise-assigned users setting determines enabled/disabled defaults for delegated policies affecting directly assigned users.
DOCS-ENTPOL-008: Generally, policies govern users licensed by the corresponding Business/Enterprise organization or enterprise, not everyone who accesses its repositories.
DOCS-ENTPOL-009: Some explicitly described policies govern everyone in enterprise repositories, including blocking cloud agent; this is a scope exception to seat-based governance.
DOCS-ENTPOL-010: Across differently configured organizations in one enterprise, the least-restrictive policy usually applies, with policy-specific exceptions.
DOCS-ENTPOL-011: Across licenses from different enterprises, the most-restrictive policy almost always applies, with exceptions; any-enterprise disabling of GitHub Chat is the example.

DOCS-ENTPOL-012: For model policies on a Team plan, model access is determined by the organization paying for usage rather than a universal multi-license rule. DOCS-ENTPOL-013: Usage billed to on the Copilot features page is the described route for identifying that paying organization; no billing state is observed.

DOCS-ENTPOL-014: The page states an individual plan is cancelled when the user joins Business/Enterprise, preventing the described personal/enterprise policy conflict; actual plan transition remains unverified.
DOCS-ENTPOL-015: The policy-conflicts reference is required for per-policy exceptions; usually/almost-always rules are insufficient for a universal evaluator.
DOCS-ENTPOL-016: Unconfigured GA feature/model defaults are supplied by a separately reviewed reusable; explicit settings and defaults are distinct.
DOCS-ENTPOL-017: The linked default-availability concept requires independent review, not certification through a link.
DOCS-ENTPOL-018: Policies can cover authenticated Copilot use in IDEs, GitHub website and CLI, but this statement is not complete per-policy surface coverage.
DOCS-ENTPOL-019: Not every policy applies on every surface; assess the supported-surfaces reference independently.
DOCS-ENTPOL-020: GitHub Copilot app and Copilot CLI have separate independent client policies, allowing one without the other.
DOCS-ENTPOL-021: Excess policy-setting access and unclear governance communication can cause drift; compliance risk is not proof that a target has drifted.
DOCS-ENTPOL-022: Regular review of policy administrators is recommended; enterprise and organization permissions must be examined separately.
